public_rationale: The contract counts the forecast as supported if, in 2025, leaders or companies defined AGI by economic or financial measures, or loosened or dismissed the term. In a February 2025 interview, Microsoft's CEO said general intelligence milestones are not the real indicators of AI progress. He called self-claiming an AGI milestone "nonsensical benchmark hacking" and said "the real benchmark is the world growing at 10%" (e1). That is an economic framing. In August 2025, Fortune reported that Microsoft was pushing to remove a contract clause tied to an OpenAI board declaration of AGI. It also cited a Wired report on an internal OpenAI debate over whether a paper on measuring AI progress could complicate a declaration of AGI (e2). These reports show AGI being handled in commercial and contractual terms during 2025. No counterevidence was found.
limitations: 'Play games' is evaluative. The assessment treats prominent economic framings or dismissals of the term as enough, and it does not judge anyone's motives.
The Microsoft and OpenAI clause details in e2 are press reports ('reportedly'), not the contract text.

The evidence does not directly show what the contractual AGI definition was during 2025. e3 records a February 2026 statement that the definition was unchanged and refers to a December 2024 report that the definition was profit-based.
